question.text: This economic and social campaign beginning in 1958 sought to rapidly transform China from an agrarian economy to modern communist society. It failed miserably.
question.clue: Millions of people were encouraged to set up backyard furnaces during this campaign.

swap.leadin: Since 2012, part of this body of water has been officially defined by a bordering nation as the "West Philippine Sea."
swap.text: Name this sea, a section of the Pacific Ocean, where the Nine-Dash Line marks a major territory claim.
swap.answerHtml: South China Sea (accept Nan Hai or Nan Zhongguo Hai)

question.text: This military leader of the Kuomintang led the Northern Expedition at the start of the Chinese Civil War. He later led the Republic of China's exiled government on Taiwan.
question.clue: This leader carried out the Northern Expedition but was kidnapped in the Xi'an incident, which forced him to agree to a united front against Japanese invasion.

swap.text: Rustichello da Pisa wrote a travelogue about this man's journey to China, where he lived in the court of Kublai Khan.
swap.clue: Two Dominican monks and gifts from Pope Gregory X were carried east by Maffeo and Niccolo, who were this man's uncle and father, respectively.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about European involvement in China during the 19th century.
question.text: Until her death in 1908, this former concubine effectively controlled Qing [pr. "Cing"] China. This mother of the Tongzhi Emperor rejected the suggestions of the Hundred Days of Reform after China was defeated in the Sino-Japanese war.
question.clue: This leader instigated a set of reformist "New Policies" at the urging of Yuan Shikai ("y'wen shu-kye"), despite having arrested the Guangxu ("gwong-shoo") emperor and purged most promoters of the Hundred Days Reform a few years prior.

swap.text: The Gansu Braves joined this anti-Western rebellion opposed by the Eight Nation Alliance. The Seymour Expedition lifted the Siege of the International Legations during this rebellion.
swap.answerHtml: Boxer Rebellion (accept Society of Righteous and Harmonious Fists, accept Yìhéquán)
swap.clue: The International Legations were besieged during this conflict that arose out of resentment over unequal treaties such as those of Wangxia and Nanking.

question.leadin: A group of these people called the Ten Attendants assassinated Emperor Shao's uncle, He Jin.
question.text: Name these people who served as court attendants and gained enormous power towards the end of the Han Dynasty. Their notorious corruption may have been an invention of later historians.
question.clue: In the Ottoman court, they were divided into black and white groups, with the chief black one controlling access to the Sultan, and in Assyria they included the rab-sa-resi (rab-sha-re-shi).

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about a Chinese dynasty.
swap.text: The Tang golden age was brought to an end by this rebellion named for its leader, an ex-Tang general, who established the rival Yan Dynasty with his lieutenant Shi Siming. It was one of the costliest wars in human history.
swap.clue: Poet Li Bai was exiled for his support of the perpetrators of this rebellion, while the Uighur intervention led to the downfall of its Yan Dynasty.

question.text: This Muslim mariner led a 1405 naval expedition to the "Western Oceans" that included stops in Sri Lanka and East Africa.
question.answerHtml: Zhèng Hé (“jung huh”) [or Ma He; or Cheng Ho; or Ma Sanbao; prompt on Zheng]
question.clue: This diplomat was given a giraffe and a zebra while taking tribute from Malindi and the Swahili coast.

swap.leadin: Name these things from U.S.-Asia relations.
swap.text: This doctrine, formulated by John Hay, demanded that all countries be given equal access to commerce in China and that only China itself could collect taxes on merchants.
swap.clue: This policy formulated by Secretary of State John Hay, which also stated that China's independence should be respected and all nations should have equal access to trade in China.

question.text: The massive naval battle of Red Cliffs pitted Cao Cao ("tsao tsao") against Liu Bei ("l'yoh bay"), two veterans of a Daoist revolt against the Han named for yellow examples of these clothing items. The Yuan dynasty collapsed after revolts named for red examples of these items.
question.answerHtml: turbans [or jīn; or tóujīn accept scarves; accept Yellow Turban Rebellions or Red Turban Rebellions]
question.clue: The name for the Qizilbash refers to a distinctive type of this object they possessed.

swap.leadin: In 69 AD, Rome was ruled by this number of emperors in succession.
swap.text: Name this number of co-emperors who ruled in the Diocletian-established Tetrarchy.
swap.clue: The Algerian War of Independence led to the collapse of the French republic of this number. The Knights Templar were disbanded under a French king of this regnal number nicknamed "The Fair."

question.leadin: The battle of Xiaoyao Ford during this period raised the reputation of Zhang Liao.
question.text: Name this period of Chinese history which ended with the defeat of Sun Hao at Jianye. This period was presaged by the Yellow Turban Rebellion.
question.clue: In the lead up to this period, one side lost the Battle of Red Cliffs.

swap.leadin: He shares his name with the Tang emperor who was the husband of Empress Wu and conquered Korea in 668.
swap.text: Name this emperor who ruled from 1127 to 1187, using his general Yue Fei to hold off the invasions of the Juchen and fortify the southern part of the former empire.

question.text: In 2007, Baumgartner became the first person to BASE jump off of this building, which is named for its number of floors.

swap.text: Exaggerated accounts of King Zhou's reign come from this history written by Sima Qian ("SUH-mah chee-EN"). It spans from the reign of the Yellow Emperor to Emperor Wu.
swap.clue: This text describes the melting of thousands of enemy weapons to create twelve colossal metal statues, a loyalty test in which a man points to a deer and calls it a horse, and the "rectification of weights and measures."

question.leadin: This building was heavily looted in 1959 after thousands of protestors gathered in front of it during Women's Uprising Day.
question.text: The white section of what building, the Potrang Karpo, became a seat of government in 1649? The red section, the Potrang Marpo, was added in the 1690s.

swap.leadin: Excavations at these people's tomb in Tuerji Mountain uncovered the remains of a priestess wearing a golden headdress and bells on her ankles.
swap.text: Name these people, whose leader Yelu Deguang established the Liao dynasty after capturing Kaifeng. In the 600s, these people formed the Dahe Confederacy to resist Tang rule.
swap.clue: They divided their holdings into the Northern and Southern Chancellories and their emperors included men such as Shengzong and Jingzong, while their first ruler took the name Taizu and was known as Abaoji.

question.leadin: Many of these things were made using tortoise shells and they were plunged into fires to see how they would crack.
question.text: Name these objects used in ancient China that people believed showed the future.
question.clue: Eventually supplanted by the I Ching, these objects were used for divination via plastromancy, scapulimancy, and pyromancy.

swap.leadin: This dynasty carried on extensive border wars with the Song Dynasty, and had a two separate government systems for the nomadic tribes of the north and its Chinese subjects in the south.
swap.text: Name this dynasty of Khitans that was toppled by the Jurchen in 1125.
swap.clue: After the demise of this dynasty, Yelu Dashi fled to Central Asia and established a successor state.
